title: Finding a vendor by their website still works
refs: SV-9160 (INV-05; V1 baseline MEASURED on the live product 15 September 2026; PRD 1.5 s4 omits vendor website - PO DECISION)
custom_preconds:
BEFORE YOU START — a five-second check that the test data is there. Open global search and type ZZAUTOTEST. You should get several groups of results — Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales.
If you get nothing at all, a new build has wiped our test data. Stop, and ask for the test data to be put back — it is one command and takes about a minute.
Do NOT create the records yourself. Records made by hand come out slightly different every time — a different postcode, a different spelling — and a test that passes against the wrong data is worse than one that fails, because it tells you everything is fine when nothing was really checked.
You only need this check ONCE at the start of a testing session, not before every case.

1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
2. The Global Search regression dataset is seeded - values in seed-data.json (build/global-search/v1-coverage-audit-2026-09-10). Every keyword below is unique to one field, so a hit proves that field is searchable.
3. Vendor 'ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply' has website 'kestrelsupply-zzt.com'. To see it for yourself: open global search, type ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel, open the supplier from the Vendors group, and read the line marked Website on its record.
4. Vendor & Order Management access: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the vendor website: kestrelsupply-zzt.com
3. Read the Vendors group.
4. Clear the input and type the customer website: bridgeporthauling-zzt.com
5. Read the Customers group.

Step 4 is there on purpose. A website is a website; if one kind of company is found by it and the other is not, that difference is the finding, and you cannot see it by testing only one.
custom_expected:
Step 2 returns the vendor 'ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply' under the Vendors group, and step 4 returns the customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling' under the Customers group.
If the vendor half returns nothing, RUN THIS TEST - do not skip it. Mark the case FAILED and write down exactly what you typed and what came back. It worked in the previous version, so it has to work here - failing is a fault and a ticket is raised against it.
A website is empty on many real records, so if either half returns nothing, open that company's record and check the Website line is actually filled in before you record a result - an empty field proves nothing about the search.

---
SOURCE - THIS CASE IS TESTED AGAINST V1, NOT AGAINST THE V2 SPECIFICATION.
This is the expected behaviour as per the V1 product itself, and it was MEASURED rather than read: on 15 September 2026 the website kestrelsupply-zzt.com was typed into the search box of the live product at https://app.shopview.com (version v26.36.7-cf5012e) and it returned ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply. The customer website was typed in the same sitting and returned its customer. The supplier's own record on the live product shows the website on screen, so the field is filled in there.
For this V1 regression suite the shipped V1 product IS the specification (Standing Rule 109). Epic SV-9160 is the project this work belongs to, not the source of this expectation, and anything quoted below from the V2 requirements is context only - never the authority for this case. The Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 lists name, telephone, email, address and city among the Vendor indexed fields and does NOT list website, so this is a code-versus-document conflict: Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as the default and Standing Rule 58 makes the conflict a PO DECISION ITEM.
This case exists because the suite had a customer-website case and no vendor one, which is why the vendor half went unnoticed until 15 September 2026.
AUTOMATION: READY - Last checked against the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 15/9/2026
